 Society Taiwan gas demand set to outstrip winter supply capacity
 State-owned CPC faces rising demand as government price controls strain market
   Oct. 31, 2026 13:31
 A worker handles a cooking gas cylinder. (CNA photo)
 1164 TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — State-owned oil company CPC Corp. said Saturday that winter cooking gas demand could exceed its monthly supply capacity of 90,000 tonnes, adding to pressure from government price controls.
 CNA reported that CPC Spokesperson Lin Ko-ju (林珂如) said demand for liquefied petroleum gas, widely used for cooking in homes and restaurants, is expected to peak between December and January. She said the company would give priority to domestic supplies and do its best to meet demand.
 CPC expanded its facilities in Shenao, New Taipei, last year, raising its maximum monthly supply to 90,000 tonnes. The company sold about 678,000 tonnes of cooking gas from January to September, accounting for more than 90% of the domestic market.
 The expected rise in demand comes as the government keeps household cooking gas prices at the same rate until the end of the year. The policy aims to protect consumers from rising fuel costs but has placed financial pressure on suppliers, per Economic Daily News.
 CPC has raised cooking gas prices by just NT$3.15 (10 cents) per kilogram since December 2020. Taiwan Petroleum Workers' Union Chair Chen Chia-lin (陳嘉麟) said the company was absorbing NT$23.75 per kilogram in costs to keep its selling price at NT$20.01.
 National Federation of Liquefied Gas Fuel Commercial Associations Chair Lai Fang-chuan (賴芳泉) said CPC sold gas for NT$1.80 less per kilogram than private supplier Formosa Petrochemical. The price gap has driven more dealers to CPC, where supplies have struggled to keep pace with demand, per CTS News .
 Lai said dealers who buy from Formosa Petrochemical must either absorb the higher cost or risk losing customers by raising prices. The problem is especially serious in central Taiwan, where competition is strong and profit margins are tight.
 Taiwan has more than 2,300 gas retailers and 110 plants that fill gas cylinders, Lai said. More than 10 retailers have closed this year, while some filling plants have merged in recent years to cut costs.
 Lai warned that the supply gap could widen as winter and year-end holidays drive up demand. He urged CPC to increase supplies and called on the government to bring prices charged by the two producers closer together.
 Energy Administration Deputy Director-General Chen Chung-hsien (陳崇憲) said the government would work with suppliers to keep gas supplies stable throughout winter. He said officials would seek to prevent shortages despite pressure on the market, per Rti .
